protocol: D-000 new cycle, turn 2 of 3; refute not confirm; records the accepted DR-005 preview Route B disposition draft plus an adopted rider
summary: Both turn-1 findings are repaired, and the second by a route stronger than either I proposed. The verdict-class defect is not merely corrected but negated in terms — the decision-type line now reads 'Codex verdict was ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES, not ACCEPT' — and clause 1 extends the foreclosure to cover both verdict classes rather than only the one it previously named. For the misplaced advisory I had offered two routes, a v3 of the disposition or recording v2 with a carve-out stated; the entry takes neither and instead makes the rider operative disposition text, conditioning condition-1 discharge on the owners recording v2 plus the rider. That is better than the carve-out I suggested, because it changes what must be recorded rather than merely disclosing what is missing. I verified the rider restores exactly the sentence v2 dropped, with the same D-032 BLK-6 citation, plus a strengthening. D-040 and D-041 are confirmed ADOPTED and are not superseded — the token supersede occurs zero times.

turn1Findings.C2-D039-01: LANDED-VERIFIED, and stronger than my proposed fix. I offered restating in adopted D-035's form or adopting D-038's parenthetical. The entry does something more direct: the decision-type line drops the 'independent ACCEPT' phrasing entirely and states 'Records an independently reviewed disposition draft. Codex verdict was ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES, not ACCEPT.' The input table names the advisory by id, RB-DR005-V2-A1. Two further corrections follow from it that I did not ask for: clause 1 now forecloses both classes — 'An ACCEPT or ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES verdict is not owner recording' — and the rejected alternative is updated from 'Treat ACCEPT as owner recording' to 'Treat ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES as owner recording', which is the class actually in play. ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES now occurs four times across the decision-type line, the table, clause 1 and the alternatives, and nowhere is the Codex verdict called ACCEPT.
turn1Findings.C2-D039-02: LANDED-VERIFIED, by a third route. My finding was that the accepted advisory restored the fail-closed guarantee into the recording entry rather than into the instrument the owners record, and I proposed either a v3 or an explicit carve-out. The entry instead makes the rider part of what must be recorded. The Subject line reads 'route-b.DR-005.preview-disposition.v2.json plus the adopted rider in clause 2'; clause 2 states the rider verbatim and adds 'The rider is operative disposition text, not a note on this entry alone'; clause 3 conditions discharge — 'Condition 1 does not discharge until those owners record v2 plus the rider'; and the alternatives reject 'Leave the fail-closed sentence only in this register entry. Rejected (C2-D039-02).' The composite is therefore asserted in four independent places and nothing in the entry undercuts it. I checked the rider's content rather than its placement alone: v1's dropped sentence was 'Fail-closed if the class is denied (adopted D-032 BLK-6)', and the rider restores that with the same citation while adding 'this disposition supplies no grant or class admission', which is a strengthening rather than a paraphrase.
turn1Findings.NOTE-D039-01: Recorded by the entry as adoption-time recording. Not mine; I did not read the Codex turn-1 verdict at any point and take no position on it beyond noting that the entry accounts for it.

whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: f59a10cffc225361c893b91c6add9cc436890dae16df5c79f2a8f419c6d002bb both times. No drift.

The Codex verdict is no longer called ACCEPT anywhere, which is the first named axis. Measured: the string ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES occurs four times, and no clause characterizes the Codex verdict as a plain ACCEPT.

The rider is asserted as disposition text rather than as an entry note, which is the second named axis, and the assertion is consistent across the Subject line, clause 2, clause 3 and the rejected alternative. The operative consequence is carried by clause 3 rather than by the assertion alone: discharge is conditioned on recording v2 plus the rider, so an owner cannot record v2 by itself and claim condition 1.

The rider's content is accurate against both the sentence it restores and the adopted decision it cites. v1's P-005-2 ended 'Fail-closed if the class is denied (adopted D-032 BLK-6)'; adopted D-032's decision text carries 'fail-closed if that class is denied' for doctor's operational-metadata write, which I re-measured under whitespace normalization because the phrase is line-wrapped in the register. The rider matches both.

ACCEPT is not treated as owner recording, and the coverage is now complete across verdict classes: clause 1 states 'This is not owner recording. An ACCEPT or ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES verdict is not owner recording', and 'not owner recording' occurs twice in the entry.
No silent SATISFIED: two occurrences, both negative — clause 3's 'DR-005 stays HARD-BLOCKED / not SATISFIED' and the rejected alternative 'Mark SATISFIED.'
Condition 1 is not discharged; conditions 2 through 5 are preserved with condition 5 named as the only implementation authorization. Implementation is not authorized anywhere.
File 08 is not edited: clause 4 states 'Does not edit file 08 (MF-6)'.

D-040 and D-041 are not superseded, and the entry's claim about their standing is true. The token supersede occurs zero times. Both are recorded ADOPTED 2026-08-13 in COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md, at the headings I located directly, so the Subject line's parenthetical 'those two are already ADOPTED' is accurate rather than assumed.

The digests I can check are correct. My turn-1 verdict is pinned at 55ae27a97d7744ed7d8d66ac4241b0e9fff8ed694db074b775355695f51ca723, matching my measurement; my v2 disposition verdict at 479b3a19 with the ACCEPT 0/0 characterization, which is what I returned; the disposition v2 at 3b50bcf1; file 08 at 877e36d3. The COORDINATOR pin is 22ba0203043ed8d9948b2a6738aaaa7f333ba206139e9567de7e916906788817, which is the current value after the D-040/D-041 adoption at 56973db moved that file, so the entry re-measured rather than carrying its turn-1 pin forward.

The two Codex digests are correct — the v2 disposition verdict at 4dc772de and the D-039 turn-1 verdict at 72f20b3a4aa1402b03bf3c6ee8456e2f28786c429954b0ecfa092d6b87676664 — both confirmed by hashing those files without opening them.

Examined and declined to raise: the linkage between the disposition and the rider runs one way. D-039 names v2, but v2's frozen bytes carry no pointer to D-039, so a reader of the disposition in isolation cannot discover the rider. I decline to file this for three reasons. Making v2 point back requires a v3, which would change the digest this entry pins — the same circularity I recorded as unfixable in my D-038 note about v8's stale reviewStatus. I already offered the v3 route at turn 1 and the coordinator declined it in favour of a construction that binds the recording act rather than merely disclosing the gap, which is stronger. And no harm follows: the guarantee independently exists in adopted D-032, and the composite is named in the Subject line of the entry that records the disposition. Raising it would amount to re-asking for a route I offered and that was lawfully declined for a better one.
whatIDidNotCheck: The Codex turn-1 and turn-2 verdicts on D-039, and the Codex review of the v2 disposition. None read; the turn-2 file is confirmed absent at review time and the other two I hashed without opening. The entry's characterization of the Codex v2 verdict as ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES 0/1 and of RB-DR005-V2-A1's content is therefore unverified by me; I verified the underlying defect from the disposition's own v1 and v2 bytes instead.
Whether the Evidence, storage and operability authorities will record v2 plus the rider.
The merits of the v2 disposition, which I reviewed separately and accepted.
Whether a v3 would still be preferable to the composite. That is a coordinator judgement between two lawful routes, and the one chosen binds more than the one I proposed.

environment.note: The subject and review prompt are untracked working-tree files at review time; digests bind working-tree bytes, not committed objects. Recorded as a condition of review, not a finding, since the draft is pre-adoption and binds nothing.
environment.measurementTool: shasum -a 256, including hashing both Codex verdicts without opening them; whitespace-normalized grep to re-verify line-wrapped phrases in adopted D-032 and in the entry's own Subject line; awk extraction of the D-040 and D-041 status lines; python3 field reads of the v1 and v2 dispositions; token sweeps

consentNote: I CONSENT with zero findings, and I record what I attacked rather than resting on an empty list. Both repairs exceed what I proposed: the verdict-class fix negates the wrong claim in terms and extends the foreclosure to the class that was actually returned, and the placement fix binds the recording act instead of disclosing the gap, which was the weaker of my two suggestions. I verified the rider against the sentence it restores and against adopted D-032 rather than accepting its self-description, and I confirmed the D-040 and D-041 adoption claims against the register rather than the draft. The one thing I found and deliberately did not file — that v2's frozen bytes cannot point back at the rider — is recorded with its reasoning, because manufacturing a note to avoid an empty finding list would be worse than an empty list with stated coverage.
